text:
Maya: quick Q — after shifting 10% to fallback-quantized I saw p95 on /v1/generate jump ~220ms; p50 barely moved and p99 moved more. Sample count in the widget looked stable. artifact or attribution bug?

Devin: are those sample counts coming from the same rollup origin? endpoint-level rollups drop variant/routing tags so we might be merging different sources.

Sanjay: saw the same pattern on Friday. our quantized path samples at a lower rate. merging percentiles without provenance can cause seemingly odd jumps when weights change.

Maya: console logs show route=generate variant=quantized for the requests hitting fallback, but the percentiles widget is endpoint-level only. you have to drill into route table to see variants.

Jorge: can you paste the exact dashboard expression? might be tdigest merge vs histogram behavior.

Maya: the p95 query is: ```quantile_over_time(0.95, latency_ms{endpoint=\"/v1/generate\"}[5m])``` — no route_weight or variant tag.

Devin: yep. when routing policy shifts 10% to the fallback the endpoint-level tdigest blobs get merged and the resulting quantile can move non-linearly. small weight changes can create large p95 deltas depending on shard distributions.

Sanjay: tdigest merges are deterministic but sensitive to input shapes. if shard A has lots of short requests and shard B has a few long tails, moving weight toward B increases p95 disproportionally.

Lee: implementation note: ingest rollup intentionally drops routing_policy metadata (sample_origin=\"ingest\") to control cardinality. that was a conscious trade for dashboard performance. maybe too lossy for percentile fidelity.

Maya: so we have options: 1) keep low-card rollup and show a warning when route weights changed; 2) surface per-route/per-variant percentiles (costly); 3) add a small provenance pill on p50/p95/p99 showing sample-count split by variant.

Jorge: i prefer 3 for UX. tiny pill next to each percentile: \"origin: merged (n=12.1k)\" with quick expand to counts by variant and a \"show by variant\" action.

Devin: backend-wise we can attach a compact provenance map to tdigest rollups with sample counts per tag. UI can use counts to highlight sensitivity without storing full high-card series. proto sketch: 
```
message Rollup {\n  bytes tdigest = 1;\n  map<string,int64> sample_counts_by_variant = 2; // e.g. {\"quantized\":1200, \"default\":10800}\n}\n```
This stays small but lets the UI show n-by-variant.

Sanjay: also consider including last_rollout_weights + timestamp in the rollup metadata so the UI can automatically flag recent weight shifts as likely causes.

Maya: who owns the rollup proto? @Devin? we'll also need a small docs blurb for SLO owners to watch \"sample-count stability\".

Devin: i'll own it. plan: proto change, aggregator populates counts map, UI reads it. add a config toggle so teams can opt into full per-variant rollups if they need absolute fidelity.

Lee: ops concern: cardinality spike. the provenance map is a good middle ground; adding full variant timeseries across all endpoints would be expensive. i'll run a cost estimate once i see the PR diff.

Jorge: UX ask: when route weights change within the last N minutes show an orange badge on the percentile: \"percentile sensitive to recent routing changes\" with a link to docs and an inline \"Show by variant\" quick action.

Maya: +1. also add a console quick-query: \"Show percentile by variant\" that runs a fast split when the provenance map is present.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: telemetry-rollup-provenance v1 -> staging :rocket:

Devin: i'll open the PR for the proto + ingest side. fallback behavior: if provenance map missing UI shows \"provenance unavailable\" and keeps current view.

Maya: please add a short doc blurb in the console: \"Interpreting p50/p95/p99 when routing or quota policies change\" — customers ask about this weekly. include one before/after example.

Sanjay: i'll draft the blurb after the PR merges. will include numbers + a small ascii diagram demonstrating sensitivity.

Maya: action items: Devin - proto + PR; Lee - cost impact estimate; Jorge - mock pill & tooltip + orange-badge state; Sanjay - doc blurb. tagging: @Devin @Lee @Jorge @Sanjay

Lee: noted. i'll start with a back-of-envelope and refine after PR.

Maya: thanks all. i'll follow up with the screenshot of the p95 jump and the routing timeline for context.
